audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0-2 read 'Skill' in the full layer against 'Karma' in content win[] and the packet chart. Rows 3-6 disagree across layers on a deeper problem: the content whys are written on a different row schema (whys[3]='Level 4', whys[4]='Level 5', whys[5]='level 6') than the full labels (Levels 4-5, Level 6, First item, 2+ items).
audit.why: Karma's 950 Q against a 725 Ice Shard and a 450 Ring of Frost wins levels 1-3 outright, so rows 0-2 are safely Karma. The row-3-to-6 offset cannot be resolved from the kits — either the content whys are mislabelled or the full labels are.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-2 flipped to Karma as one group. Rows 3-6 deliberately left alone and raised as a question.

notes: Chart: rows 0-2 flipped from 'Skill' to 'Karma' to match content win[] and the packet chart (win[] already holds Karma, so no paired content edit exists to write). Rows 3-6 LEFT ALONE deliberately — the two layers are not merely disagreeing, they are on different row schemas: content whys[3]/[4]/[5] are written as 'Level 4' / 'Level 5' / 'level 6' while the full labels are 'Levels 4-5' / 'Level 6' / 'First item'. Aligning sides without knowing which schema is canonical would create a row whose why argues the opposite verdict. phases[4].why was rewritten in place (side unchanged at Lissandra) because it described Karma's own level 6 under a Lissandra verdict. phases[5] (side 'Skill') and phases[6] (side 'Lissandra') still carry whys describing Karma winning; I did not touch them for the same schema reason. Packet flags the win rate (39.56%) against a Karma-favoured chart — plausible for a lane-strong/scaling-weak pairing, but the schema question should be settled first.
